newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay index ends 1.47 pct up, focus on blue.
newsitem.headline: Bombay index ends 1.47 pct up, focus on blue.

text.p: Bombay's blue chip stocks staged a small rally towards close of trade on Thursday boosted by a spate of speculative buy orders, traders said.
"It's sheer speculation and playing by punters. There was very thin trade on the foreign fund action," said Ashith Kampani, head of dealing at JM Share & Stock Brokers.
Institutional activity however remained dull due to the closure of many Asian markets on Wednesday on account of the Chinese New Year which affected trade, dealers said.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) 30-share index ended 49.39 points up at 3,404.11, the intra-day high after a weak start.
The market has seen a roller-coaster ride after the government last week failed to come up with promised confidence-boosting measures.
Traders expect the volatility to continue on abounding speculation about government policies expected in the 1997 budget due on February 28.
"Vibrancy and volatility in shares are likely till the budget. Action is mainly on top stocks," said JM's Kampani.
Shares of Gujarat Ambuja Cements added 3.50 rupees, or 1.45 percent, to 244.75 after it announced a 20 percent jump in first half net profit to 489.8 million rupees, ending December 1996.
Brokers said domestic funds were eager sellers at higher levels but investors were waiting for a clear picture to emerge before making fresh commitments in the market.
In the list of pivotal stocks, SBI rose 8.0 rupees to 269.50, TISCO 6.0 to 187.50, Reliance 8.25 to 269.50, ITC 6.25 to 384.50 and TELCO 6.75 to 319.0.
The NSE's 50-stock index closed 9.75 points or 1.01 percent higher at a provisional 972.25.
